generatedBy: hand-maintained; Reference/MDN has no extractor yet
policy: A reference document is retired once every name it defines is accounted for by the compiler, and the coverage tests exercise it. For an element or an attribute that means the name is registered, validated on the elements MDN says accept it, and routed to a typed native property; for a CSS property it means the compiler compiles it. A name that is only mentioned is not enough. The retired file is deleted and the deletion is recorded here, so the reference shrinks and the compiler's knowledge of what it once stated does not.
scope: The CSS and HTML reference material under Reference/MDN/files/en-us/web: css/reference/{properties,selectors,at-rules,values}, html/reference/{elements,attributes,global_attributes}. The rest of the MDN content repository (Web API, JavaScript, HTTP, and so on) is outside this compiler's subject.

Custom properties are substituted before a declaration's value is parsed, so a reference can stand in for a whole value, an operand of a function, or a fallback: `calc(var(--gap) * 2)` and `var(--missing, 7px)` both compile. The substitution descends into a function's arguments and is inherited by descendants, and a chain longer than sixteen links is reported as a cycle rather than followed.

notes: The CSS Working Group drafts and the WHATWG HTML drafts were consumed before this reference arrived, so the compiler already accounts for 1,080 CSS property names and the HTML vocabulary those drafts define. Reference/MDN is a second, differently structured reference: one Markdown page per item, which is why it is walked page by page rather than mined by an extractor.

A property name the compiler carries is known, parsed and stored but not compiled: it keeps its declared value and is reported as an unimplemented feature (RCC010) rather than refused. Implementing one means compiling it and giving it its rendering behaviour.

The 59 CSS property names MDN has that no draft of the reference defined are the vendor-prefixed set, the legacy flexbox box-* set, the SVG presentation attributes (which are SVG attribute vocabulary, not CSS properties) and touch-action, math-*, corner-*-shape, user-modify and font-smooth.

The out-of-flow model (position, top, right, bottom, left, inset, z-index) was the first slice of the layout machinery: the offsets and the shorthand are compiled and lowered, layout shifts relative and sticky boxes and places absolute and fixed boxes against their containing block, and a fixed box is pinned to the viewport through scrolling in paint, hit testing and bounds.

The float model (float, clear) was the second slice of the layout machinery: both are compiled and lowered, a float is placed shrink-to-fit against its side and its container grows to contain it, the line boxes crossing it lose its width, and clear drops a box below the floats it names.

The flex model (display: flex, flex-direction, flex-wrap, flex-flow, justify-content, align-items, align-content, align-self, flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, order, gap, row-gap and column-gap) is the third slice of the layout machinery. The container lays its items along one axis, breaks them into lines when flex-wrap allows it, distributes free space by the growth factors, shrinks when they overflow, sorts them by order, spaces them and their lines with gap, and shares the free cross space between the lines with align-content. The one part of the model still carried rather than compiled is the `flex` shorthand over flex-grow, flex-shrink and flex-basis; its page stays until it is expanded.

The compiled property pages that predate the MDN walk were then read one by one and checked against the compiler, because a property implemented before the reference arrived was implemented from the specification, not from MDN. Every value, initial value, inherited flag and specification citation was compared. The pass found real divergences and they were fixed: `white-space` had no answer for the collapse and wrap keywords the page now gives, `font-style` refused `oblique`, `overflow` refused `overlay`, `writing-mode` and `text-orientation` refused their deprecated spellings, and `text-decoration-thickness` and `text-underline-offset` cited `css-text-decor-3` where the reference now states them in `css-text-decor-4`. The pages whose values are still partly unanswered -- display, which names the grid values the compiler does not compile; text-indent, whose `each-line` and `hanging` are not implemented; text-transform, whose `full-width`, `full-size-kana` and `math-auto` are not; and text-decoration-line, whose `spelling-error` and `grammar-error` are not -- stay in the reference until those values have an answer.

The numeric functions are the reference's second family of values that are not properties. They are implemented in the same compiled math program as calc(): a step names the function and the number of operands it takes, and a program whose operands are all absolute folds at compile time to a number, a length or an angle. The type rules are the reference's, so `sin(30deg)` is the number 0.5, `hypot(3px, 4px)` is 5px, `atan2(1, 1)` is an angle and `calc(2px * 3px)` is refused. Two bugs were found and fixed while implementing them: a function nested inside another function was never parsed (the parser counted the nested block twice and reported the outer one as unclosed), and a var() inside a function was never substituted, so `calc(var(--gap) * 2)` did not compile. The functions the reference defines that need a document or a runtime rather than arithmetic -- anchor(), anchor-size(), attr(), calc-size(), counter(), counters(), element(), env(), if(), progress(), random(), sibling-count(), sibling-index(), the image functions and the grid functions minmax(), repeat() and fit-content() outside a size -- stay in the reference until they have an answer.
